_about: What the personal-data check (scripts/ci/no-personal-data.mjs) lets through. Read docs/RUNBOOK.md, 'What may never be committed', before adding anything here. Every entry needs a note saying why it cannot be a person. A pull request that touches this file is read line by line.
_skipPaths: package-lock.json holds hashes only. This file holds, by design, the values it allows (a company's published number and mailboxes, the invented pins), so it cannot be scanned against itself: that is why a change to it is read line by line, and test/ci/fixtures-invented.test.ts checks its shape.

phones._about: An invented range is a prefix of the number with its country code, at most 1,000 numbers wide (8 digits for an 11-digit number), unless it is reserved: no operator can assign it. Test files take their numbers from here.

ranges.note: +961 70 000 xxx: the project's standard fake block since the first fixtures (H1 confirmed it for the Kapso fixtures)
+961 70 009 xxx: fake block next to the standard one, used by the Worker end-to-end test and the webhook-events test
+961 70 300 xxx: fake block used by the receiving-margin test only
+961 70 400 xxx: fake block used by the recall test only
+961 70 999 xxx: fake block used by the console day-close test only
+961 71 000 xxx: fake block used by the hub and ops test kits
+961 71 990 xxx: fake block used by the reply-speed test only
+961 71 999 xxx: fake block used by the ordering test only
+961 00 000 xxx: no Lebanese operator has a 00 prefix, so the number cannot exist (a stand-in for the shop's own link in the catalog tests)
+44 7700 900xxx: Ofcom's range for drama and fiction; it is never assigned to a subscriber
+999 is not assigned as a country code, so no number that starts with it can exist (the simulated customers in evals/sim)
